t: The Swedish army had shrunk to 20,000 soldiers and 34 cannons by spring 1709, after a campaign through Russian scorched earth and the coldest winter in Europe in over 500 years, while Peter brought 75,000 to 80,000 men.

Charles XII was wounded in the foot on 20 June and could not stand, so Field Marshal Rehnskiöld led the attack, and about a third of the Swedish infantry under Roos was cut off at the redoubts before the main fight began.
Charles and Mazepa escaped to the Ottoman Empire with about 1,500 men, and the surrender at Perevolochna three days later ended the Swedish army as a field force.
dyk: Charles XII spent five years in exile at Bendery in the Ottoman Empire after Poltava, and returned to Sweden only in December 1715.
ev: Charles XII wins early victories in North Zealand and at Narva
Peter I withdraws from Poland and offers to return the occupied Baltic provinces, except Ingria; Charles refuses
The Swedish army of almost 44,000 leaves Saxony for Russia in August
Charles turns south into Ukraine to join Mazepa, and Lewenhaupt loses his supply train at Lesnaya
Charles besieges Poltava from 2 May and is wounded in the foot on 20 June
The Swedes attack the Russian redoubts before dawn and are defeated in the open field
Lewenhaupt surrenders the remaining Swedes at Perevolochna
Charles returns to Sweden in December after five years in the Ottoman Empire

f.date: 8 July 1709 (28 June in the Swedish calendar)
f.place: Near the fortress of Poltava on the Vorskla river, in present-day Ukraine
f.sides: The Russian army under Tsar Peter I, 75,000 to 80,000 men (80,000 in another account of the build-up), against a Swedish army under Field Marshal Carl Gustaf Rehnskiöld, with King Charles XII wounded, which had been reduced to 20,000 soldiers and 34 cannons by the spring
f.outcome: The Swedes were defeated and fled the field. Charles XII and Ivan Mazepa escaped with about 1,500 men, and the rest of the army surrendered at Perevolochna on 11 July 1709.
